review_locator: PMCID:PMC2897247, Transcriptional Regulation of Macrophage Polarization, STAT6/M2-marker section; PMCID:PMC3107597, Transcriptional regulation by STAT6
primary_title: Interleukin-25 fails to activate STAT6 and induce alternatively activated macrophages
decision_basis: The reviews identify MRC1 as a STAT6-dependent alternative-macrophage marker; the cited primary shows IL-4/IL-13 activate STAT6 and STAT6 silencing reduces MRC1 RNA in human CD14-positive cells.
limitations_preserved: STAT6 silencing and cytokine-response evidence support a bounded human monocyte/macrophage MRC1 gene bridge; the primary does not establish direct STAT6 occupancy at the MRC1 promoter, and MRC1 transcript does not by itself establish CD206 protein or phagocytic function.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7608745, The alternative macrophage relay: STAT6 passes the baton to EGR2; PMCID:PMC9649892, The epigenetic state of IL-4-polarized macrophages enables inflammatory cistromic expansion and extended synergistic response to TLR ligands
primary_title: The transcription factor EGR2 is the molecular linchpin connecting STAT6 activation to the late, stable epigenomic program of alternative macrophage polarization
decision_basis: The reviews identify CHIL4 as an EGR2-dependent alternative-macrophage output; the cited primary shows IL-4-induced Chil4 expression is close to absolutely dependent on Egr2 and is facilitated by inducible EGR2 in myeloid cells.
limitations_preserved: EGR2 dependence and gain-of-function support a bounded alternative-macrophage Chil4 gene bridge, but direct EGR2 occupancy at the Chil4 locus is not established in the cited primary; distinguish CHIL4 transcript from CHIL4 protein/function and do not infer SCI or terminal-TF output.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7608745, The alternative macrophage relay: STAT6 passes the baton to EGR2; PMCID:PMC8208725, Mechanisms underlying divergent responses of genetically distinct macrophages to IL-4
primary_title: Mechanisms underlying divergent responses of genetically distinct macrophages to IL-4; The transcription factor EGR2 is the molecular linchpin connecting STAT6 activation to the late, stable epigenomic program of alternative macrophage polarization
decision_basis: The reviews identify MMP12 among EGR2-associated alternative-polarization genes; the cited primary shows EGR2, STAT6 and PPAR-gamma co-binding at an IL-4-induced Mmp12 enhancer and Egr2-dependent remodeling of that regulatory region.
limitations_preserved: Enhancer co-binding and Egr2-dependent remodeling support a bounded macrophage Mmp12 gene bridge, but the cited evidence does not establish EGR2-exclusive promoter activation; preserve STAT6/PPAR-gamma cooperation and do not infer MMP12 protein activity, SCI or terminal-TF output.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7201933, Historical overview of the interleukin-6 family cytokine, IL-6 expression regulation section
primary_title: Activation of the interleukin 6 gene by Mycobacterium tuberculosis or lipopolysaccharide is mediated by nuclear factors NF-IL6 and NF-kappa B
decision_basis: The review identifies NF-kappaB as a positive regulator of IL6 transcription; the cited primary maps LPS- and mycobacterial-lipoarabinomannan-responsive IL-6 promoter activity to an NF-kappaB site and shows loss of inducibility after site-directed mutation.
limitations_preserved: NF-kappaB-site dependence supports a bounded inflammatory IL6 gene bridge, but the primary does not isolate RELA from other NF-kappaB subunits at the endogenous promoter; distinguish IL6 transcript from secreted IL-6 protein and downstream receptor signaling.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7201933, Historical overview of the interleukin-6 family cytokine, IL-6 expression regulation section
primary_title: Transcription factors NF-IL6 and NF-kappa B synergistically activate transcription of the inflammatory cytokines, interleukin 6 and interleukin 8
decision_basis: The review identifies cooperative NF-kappaB and NF-IL6/CEBPB promoter control of IL6; the cited primary shows p65 and NF-IL6/CEBPB directly associate and synergistically activate an IL-6 promoter requiring both factor-binding sites.
limitations_preserved: Direct factor association and dual-site promoter dependence support a bounded cooperative IL6 gene bridge; preserve NF-IL6/CEBPB nomenclature and do not infer IL-6 secretion, receptor signaling, SCI or terminal-TF output.
